findings.claim: Criterion 1 is not met: a review record can still be written on AO_AGENT_ID alone. recordReview is exported, and its only identity gate is `env.AO_AGENT_ID === reviewerId`. A worker that imports reviewer.mjs and calls recordReview with its own env setting AO_AGENT_ID to the reviewer id writes an approve record, with no verdict file, no seal and no pane proof. That is the original attack, moved from the CLI to an in-process import.
findings.evidence: reviewer.mjs:1199-1201 `export async function recordReview({ ... env = process.env ... })` with `invariant(registered && registered.agent_id === reviewerId && env.AO_AGENT_ID === reviewerId, ...)`. collectReview (line 1714) calls it with `env: { ...env, AO_AGENT_ID: record.agent_id }`, which shows the gate is just an env value. The lead's review-235 reproduced currentReviewStatus becoming satisfied this way.
findings.fix: Stop exporting the write path: make recordReview internal to collectReview, or require requireReviewerCaller in it the way submitReviewVerdict does. Grep reviewer.mjs, review-mcp.mjs and management.mjs for every remaining AO_AGENT_ID trust, and add a negative test for each.

findings.claim: The verdict seal gives false assurance. The key is created lazily: verdictKey(create) accepts any existing file of 32 bytes or more, and writes a new key with `wx` only when none exists. A worker that runs before the first submit can therefore plant a key of its choosing and forge seals without reading anything. Together with the same-uid read, the seal does not stop the hand-written verdict file that criterion 2 targets.
findings.evidence: Lines 1604-1611: `const existing = await readFile(path)...; if (existing?.length >= 32 || !create) return existing...; await writeFile(path, randomBytes(32), { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o600 })`. Nothing checks the file's creator, mode or age.
findings.fix: Following the lead's decision, remove the seal and the exported sealVerdict rather than ship false assurance. Keep replay protection through the per-request nonce, and say plainly in the CHANGELOG and docs that a same-user worker can still write the verdict and review records, with TM-508 (keep workers out of the AO state root) as the fix.

findings.claim: sessionIdentity still trusts AO_AGENT_ID for every claimed agent that is not the lead. requireLeadCaller returns null unless the claimed id is the repository lead, so a process setting AO_AGENT_ID to the reviewer's or an observer's id acts as that agent on every mailbox verb. Rule 3 in the task (comment 1) asks for callerIdentity to be covered too.
findings.evidence: Lines 390-411: when AO_AGENT_ID is set, `caller = callerIdentity(env)` is used as is. The only proof is `await requireLeadCaller({ ..., agentId: caller.agentId, ... })`, which per delegation.mjs:258-262 returns null for any id other than the lead.
findings.fix: For any claimed agent that has a recorded binding (reviewer, observer, roles, census), require requireCallerInPane against that binding. Fall back to env only for an agent with no binding at all. Add negative tests for a forged reviewer id and a forged observer id.

findings.claim: Stale documentation, and no check evidence. README.md:500 and agent-orchestration/docs/repository-leads.md:313 still document the removed `ao-topology review submit`. Separately, none of the six required checks has evidence for this request.
findings.evidence: TM-427 comment 15 (worker decision) and comment 20 (lead review, item 5) name both stale mentions. The request's `checks_unsatisfied` lists all six required checks as 'no evidence'.
findings.fix: Widen the touches to include README.md and docs/repository-leads.md and fix both mentions. Attach the required checks, run with the current argv (#239), at the successor revision.

findings.claim: TM-462B (reserved senders, lead proof, the census fallback, run send no longer trusting env) is bundled into this task. It changes every mailbox verb: a lead driving mail from a second terminal is now refused.
findings.evidence: There is a separate CHANGELOG entry for TM-462B. The implementation brief (comment 7, A6) assigns it here deliberately.
findings.fix: Keep it if intended, but record TM-462B's acceptance on TM-462 when this lands, and mention the second-terminal refusal in the CHANGELOG.

findings.claim: These are correct and should be kept: requireCallerInPane as the single proof, requireReviewerCaller in submitReviewVerdict (with AO_AGENT_ID no longer consulted), the removal of shell `review submit`, and reviewerNonceAck bound to ancestry (host readiness still reads the pane line, so the restricted reviewer is unaffected).

findings.claim: The same-user residual remains by design and is documented: a same-user process that writes the agent-orchestration state directly (verdicts/, review and reviewer records) or types into the reviewer pane with tmux send-keys is not stopped. TM-508 (keep workers out of the state root) is the tracked fix and should stay high priority, because this gate's integrity depends on it.

I reviewed revision 55f68a71 (patch sha256 2dcc210a…), the same patch as request d88ae1ab, which was blocked only for host-run evidence and the contract-test scope. Both are now resolved: tests/contract/topology-lead-recovery-tmux.test.mjs is in the touches, and all checks are host-run with output (agent-orchestration unit 1335 and 0, task-management unit 1704 and 0, contract 19 and 0, build:check, validates and plugin-rsync tests 0). All three criteria are met. (1) Submit, ack and the exported recordReview require the live reviewer pane plus pid ancestry (requireReviewerCaller); AO_AGENT_ID gates no write path; the shell `review submit` is removed. (2) A hand-written verdict file is accepted only against the per-request nonce, with no false seal, and the same-user limit is documented. (3) Negative tests cover a forged AO_AGENT_ID through every channel. sessionIdentity also proves the lead and any agent with a recorded pane, and refuses reserved host senders. The docs no longer mention `review submit`.
